extracted.intended_audience: applicants for FMCSA exemptions, motor carriers (pyrotechnics industry), and members of the public who will submit comments
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting or preparing an administrative comment or an exemption application (and supporting materials) for FMCSA regarding exemptions from Hours-of-Service (HOS) and ELD rules for pyrotechnics transport during Independence Day periods. Includes procedural requirements for filing, confidentiality handling, and the safety standard the Agency uses to evaluate exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include docket number, targeted section, and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit a comment, please include the docket number for this notice (FMCSA-2021-0052), indicate the specific section of this document to which the comment applies, and provide a reason for suggestions or recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FMCSA recommends including such specificity to help the Agency identify what your comment addresses and the rationale for any suggested changes; this instruction appears in the 'Submitting Comments' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only one submission method and identify agency/docket
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid duplication, please use only one of the listed methods (Federal eRulemaking Portal, Mail, Hand Delivery/Courier, Fax). Each submission must include the Agency name and the docket number (FMCSA-2021-0052) for this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice lists four acceptable submission methods and emphasizes using a single method to avoid duplicate filings; failure to include agency/docket information may impede processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contact information (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA recommends that you include your name and a mailing address, an email address, or a phone number in the body of your document so the Agency can contact you if it has questions regarding your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including contact info is recommended (not strictly required) so the Agency can follow up for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission instructions (Regulations.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit your comment online, go to https://www.regulations.gov/docket/FMCSA-2021-0052/document, click on this notice, click 'Comment,' and type your comment into the text box on the following screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments submitted via Regulations.gov are posted without change to the public docket; follow the site's interface to attach or enter comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail/hand-delivery formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit your comments by mail or hand delivery, submit them in an unbound format, no larger than 8 1/2 by 11 inches, suitable for copying and electronic filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formatting instruction ensures mailed submissions can be scanned and processed electronically; follow the size and unbound requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement and handling of late comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received on or before May 19, 2025. Comments received after the comment closing date will be filed in the public docket and will be considered to the extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission ensures full consideration; late comments are not guaranteed full consideration but will be placed in the docket and considered where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and privacy of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: DOT posts all comments received without change to www.regulations.gov, including any personal information included in a comment. The comments are posted without edit and are searchable by the name of the submitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include information you do not want publicly disclosed; the notice also references the Privacy Act and the applicable system of records (DOT/ALL-14 FDMS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) handling and marking
rubrics_metrics.description: CBI is commercial or financial information both customarily and actually treated as private by its owner. If your comments contain such information, clearly designate those pages as 'PROPIN' to indicate proprietary information; FMCSA will treat such marked submissions as confidential under FOIA and they will not be placed in the public docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions containing CBI should be sent to Brian Dahlin, Chief, Regulatory Evaluation Division (address and email provided). At this time, you need not send a duplicate hardcopy of your electronic CBI submissions to FMCSA headquarters. Any comments not specifically designated as CBI will be placed in the public docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket inspection instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: To view documents mentioned as being available in the docket, go to https://www.regulations.gov/docket/FMCSA-2021-0052 and choose the document to review. To view comments, click this notice, then click 'Browse Comments.' If you do not have internet access, you may view the docket in person at Dockets Operations (address provided) during business hours; call ahead to ensure assistance is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice provides URL and physical location plus phone numbers to arrange an in-person visit; this ensures public access to supporting materials and comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency must provide access to application-relevant information (including safety analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA must provide the public an opportunity to inspect the information relevant to the application, including any safety analyses that have been conducted (required by 49 CFR 381.315(a) and statutory authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should include or make available safety analyses and supporting materials in the docket so the Agency and public can review them; the Agency will make such materials available for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority and procedural publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA has authority under 49 U.S.C. 31136(e) and 31315(b) to grant exemptions from the FMCSRs. FMCSA must publish a notice of each exemption request in the Federal Register (49 CFR 381.315(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the statutory and regulatory framework requiring publication and public comment for exemption requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation standard for granting exemptions (safety equivalence test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency reviews safety analyses and public comments submitted and determines whether granting the exemption would likely achieve a level of safety equivalent to, or greater than, the level that would be achieved absent such exemption pursuant to the standard set forth in 49 U.S.C. 31315(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the controlling substantive standard FMCSA applies when deciding whether to grant an exemption; applicants should present evidence and analyses demonstrating equivalent or greater safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of final decision notice if granted or denied
rubrics_metrics.description: If granted, the notice will identify the regulatory provision from which the applicant will be exempt, the effective period, and all terms and conditions of the exemption (49 CFR 381.315(c)(1)). If the exemption is denied, the notice will explain the reason for the denial (49 CFR 381.315(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and commenters can expect the final Federal Register notice to explicitly state the scope, duration, and conditions of any exemption or the reasons for denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal possibility for exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The exemption may be renewed (49 CFR 381.300(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking multi-year relief should address factors relevant to renewal and demonstrate ongoing satisfaction of the equivalence-of-safety standard; the notice itself is an application for renewal of prior exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors and evidence FMCSA will likely consider (implied/illustrative from applicant's assertions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant considerations include: past experience with prior waivers/exemptions; demonstration that exemption operations achieve equivalent safety over time; training commitments (e.g., additional driver/rest training); driver qualifications and experience; proportion of actual driving time relative to allowed driving hours; operational constraints (e.g., vehicles without sleeper berths); and economic burdens of compliance (e.g., need to hire a second driver).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the notice explicitly states the legal standard (safety equivalence), the applicant's supporting arguments illustrate the types of factual and analytical evidence FMCSA will weigh in applying that standard; commenters should address these factors as appropriate.
